rows.rationale: Ibrahim already believed but asked to see how Allah gives life, so his heart would be at rest — reassurance strengthens an already-sincere but unsettled heart.
Ibrahim shown the dominion of the heavens and earth so that he would be of those with sure faith (al-muqinin).
Describes true believers as those with certainty (yuqinun) about the Hereafter — certainty as a defining trait to hold onto.
Allah's control of the heavens/sun/moon is presented so 'you may be certain of meeting your Lord' — ties creation order to certainty.
'On the earth are signs for those who have certainty (al-muqinin)' — signs exist specifically for those seeking firmer certainty.
'This is the certain Truth (haqqu l-yaqin)' — direct affirmation of certainty at the close of a surah about the Hereafter.
'This is verily the certain Truth' — parallel affirmation of certainty in Al-Haqqah.
Mandatory: the believers' hearts fear at Allah's mention and their faith increases when His verses are recited.
Mandatory: revelation increases the faith of believers, who rejoice.
Believers warned of a gathering enemy were only increased in faith, not fear — faith strengthened under pressure.
Seeing the confederate armies at the Battle of the Trench only increased the believers in faith and submission.
Allah sends tranquility into believers' hearts 'that they might add faith unto their faith.'
Explains that some matters are made trials so that believers may increase in faith and the doubtful may be free of doubt.
Mandatory: the believers' prayer that Allah not let their hearts deviate after having been guided.
Mandatory: those who say 'Our Lord is Allah' then remain steadfast receive angels' reassurance.
Parallel steadfastness verse: no fear or grief for those who affirm Allah and stand firm.
Allah confirms/stabilizes believers with the firm word, in this life and the next.
Allah strengthens the believers' hearts and makes their feet firm at a moment of real fear (Badr).
Angels sent to make believers firm, directly addressing a wavering heart in battle.
The Quran is sent down by the Holy Spirit specifically to confirm/stabilize believers.
Promise that supporting Allah's cause is met with firm footing.
Direct command to remain steadfast exactly as commanded — a well-known verse for someone needing resolve.
Mandatory: people are not left merely to say 'we believe' without being tried.
Direct continuation: those before were tried too, so Allah may know the truthful from the liars.
Believers 'shaken' (zulzilu) by hardship until asking 'when comes Allah's help?' — then reassurance that it is near. Very direct match for shaken faith.
At the Battle of the Trench believers were shaken with a mighty shaking.
Immediate continuation: 'there were the believers sorely tried.'
Believers will surely be tried in their wealth and their selves.
Every soul is tried with evil and good as a trial.
Believers will be tried until the sincere and steadfast among them are made known.
Mandatory: has the time not come for believers' hearts to soften/humble themselves to Allah's remembrance?
Skins shiver at the Quran's recitation then soften, with hearts, to the remembrance of Allah.
Hearts find rest only in the remembrance of Allah — foundational heart-softening verse.
Allah expands the chest of whoever He guides to Islam.
Whoever's chest Allah has expanded for Islam is upon a light from his Lord.
Mandatory: heavens/earth, night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, animals, winds and clouds — signs for a people who reason.
Mandatory (first half of the pair): creation of the heavens/earth and alternation of night/day are signs for people of understanding.
Mandatory (second half): those who remember Allah standing/sitting/lying down and reflect on the heavens and earth's creation.
'Have they not pondered within themselves' about the true purpose of creation.
Signs in the heavens and earth for believers.
Signs in human creation and every beast Allah scatters, for people who are certain.
Night/day, provision from the sky, and shifting winds are signs for a people who reason.
'Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built and adorned it' — invites literal looking, not just belief.
'Will they not regard the camel — how it is created?' opens the classic four-part 'do they not look' sequence.
Continuation: the sky, how it is raised.
Continuation: the mountains, how they are set up.
Continuation: the earth, how it is spread out.
Allah will show signs 'in the horizons and in themselves' until the truth becomes clear — a summary certainty verse.
Allah splits the seed and the date-stone, and brings the living from the dead.
He splits the dawn and appointed the night for stillness, sun and moon for reckoning.
Stars appointed as signs so travellers can find their way, explained for people who know.
Rain producing vegetation, grain, palm, gardens of grapes, olive and pomegranate — 'signs for a people who believe.'
Water sent down from the sky: drink for you, and pasture for your cattle.
Crops, olives, palms, grapes and every kind of fruit grown by that same water — a sign for a people who reflect.
The sea subjected: fresh meat to eat, ornaments to wear, ships cleaving it, seeking Allah's bounty.
Mountains set firm so the earth does not shake with you, and rivers/roads for guidance.
Landmarks, and by the star (also) they find guidance — ties navigation to guidance.
Rain reviving the dead earth — a sign for a people who hear.
Milk from between waste and blood, pure and pleasant to drink — a lesson.
Fruit of the date-palm and grapes, sustenance — a sign for a people who reason.
Allah inspires the bee to build in mountains, trees and structures.
Honey from the bee, a healing for people — 'a sign for a people who reflect.'
Brought out of your mothers' wombs knowing nothing, then given hearing, sight, and hearts.
Birds held poised in the sky by nothing but Allah — a sign for people who believe.
Heavens and earth were joined then split apart, and every living thing made from water.
Mountains set firm so the earth does not shake, and passes/ways made for guidance.
The sky made a canopy, yet people turn away from its signs.
Night, day, sun and moon — each floating in its own orbit.
Clouds driven, joined, then rain and hail from mountains of cloud in the sky — a sign for those with insight.
Every living creature created from water, moving in different ways — Allah creates what He wills.
Shadow extended, and how the sun is made its indicator.
Night made a garment, sleep made rest, and day made a time of rising.
Winds as heralds of mercy, and pure water sent down from the sky.
That water revives dead land and provides drink for many creatures He created.
Two seas, one sweet and one salt, with an unseen barrier between them.
Constellations placed in the sky, along with a lamp (the sun) and a shining moon.
Night and day made to succeed one another, for whoever wishes to reflect or give thanks.
Rain producing fruit of differing colors, and streaks of white/red/raven-black in the mountains.
People, beasts, and cattle likewise of differing colors — only those with knowledge truly fear/revere Allah through this.
Heavens and earth created in truth; He wraps night over day and day over night, sun and moon subjected.
Night, day, sun, and moon are among His signs; do not prostrate to the sun or moon, but to Allah.
The earth you see desolate stirs and grows when rain descends — the same power that revives it revives the dead.
The sea subjected for ships to run upon by His command, and to seek His bounty.
First of the Ar-Rum sign sequence: He created you from dust, then you became human beings spread throughout the earth.
Creation of the heavens and earth, and the diversity of languages and colors — signs for those who know.
Sleep by night and day, and seeking His bounty — signs for a people who hear.
Lightning shown as fear and hope, and rain reviving dead earth — signs for a people who reason.
Heaven and earth standing firm by His command; then one call and you emerge from the earth.
The dead earth is a sign: We revive it and bring forth grain from it, so they eat.
The night is a sign: We strip the day from it and they are left in darkness.
The sun runs to a term appointed for it — the ordaining of the Mighty, the Knower.
The moon appointed with mansions until it returns like an old shrivelled palm-leaf.
Neither sun nor moon may overtake the other, nor night outstrip the day — each floats in an orbit.
A sign for them: We carried their offspring in the laden ship.
'And in yourselves — do you not then see?' — signs within one's own self, not only the external world.
Sustenance, and what is promised, is in the heaven.
Among His signs: spouses created from among yourselves, so you find rest in them, and He placed between you love and mercy.
Allah made well everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay.
Then made his progeny from an extract of despised fluid.
Then fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and gave hearing, sight and hearts — little thanks is given.
Man created from an extract of clay — the well-known embryology-opening verse.
Then made him a drop in a firm resting-place.
The drop's stages of development, ending 'blessed is Allah, the best of creators.'
'So let man consider from what he is created.'
Created from a gushing fluid.
Cattle created for you: warmth, uses, and food.
Beauty in them, morning and evening.
Horses, mules and donkeys for riding and adornment.
'If you would count Allah's favor you could not compute it' — the central blessing-awareness verse.
Parallel verse: He gives you all that you ask Him for, and if you counted His favor you could not compute it.
Allah has subjected all that is in the heavens and earth, and completed His favor outwardly and inwardly.
He created for you all that is on the earth.
The earth made subservient — walk its regions and eat of His provision.
He produced you and gave you hearing, sight and hearts — little thanks is given.
Homes made a resting place, tents made light to carry, and wool/fur/hair for furnishing and comfort.
'This is the Book, no doubt therein, a guidance for the God-fearing' — a direct answer to doubt.
'A clear proof (burhan) has come to you from your Lord, and We have sent down a clear light.'
A light and a clear Book have come from Allah.
By it Allah guides whoever seeks His pleasure to the paths of peace, and brings them from darkness to light.
A Book sent down to bring people out of darkness into light.
This Quran guides to what is most upright.
Directly addresses doubt about resurrection, then walks through human creation stages and dead-earth revival as evidence.
The famous challenge: 'who will revive the bones when they have decayed?'
Answer: He who produced them the first time will revive them; He knows every creation.
Is not He who created the heavens and earth able to create the like of them?
He originates creation, then repeats it — easier for Him — the highest attribute belongs to Him.
As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it — a promise binding upon Him.
Disbelievers' doubt voiced: 'when we are dead and turned to dust, that is a far return.'
Reply: We know what the earth takes from them, and with Us is a book that preserves.
'Were We then worn out by the first creation? Yet they are in doubt about a new creation.'
Does man think We will not assemble his bones?
Yes — able even to restore his very fingertips.
Have they not considered that Allah, who created the heavens and earth without weariness, is able to revive the dead?
Foundational Jannah description: gardens beneath which rivers flow, for those who believe and do good.
Gardens with rivers, abiding forever, pure spouses, and Allah's pleasure.
A garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the God-fearing.
Gardens of Eden and good homes; Allah's pleasure described as the greatest bliss of all.
Believers guided by their faith; rivers flow beneath them in the Gardens of Delight (Na'im).
Their greeting therein is 'Peace.'
Gardens of Eden, entered along with righteous relatives; angels enter upon them from every gate.
Angels' greeting: 'Peace be upon you for that you patiently endured.'
Believers admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, their greeting therein 'Peace.'
Gardens of Eden they enter, with whatever they wish therein.
Angels greet the righteous at death: 'Peace be upon you, enter Paradise for what you used to do.'
Believers who do good have the Gardens of Paradise (Firdaws) as a lodging.
Abiding therein forever, never wishing to leave.
Exception for the repentant/believing/righteous: they enter Paradise without being wronged.
Gardens of Eden, promised though unseen — a promise that is fulfilled.
Such is the Paradise given as inheritance to Allah's pious servants.
Gardens of Eden, rivers flowing beneath, abiding forever — the reward for purifying oneself.
Believers adorned with gold bracelets and pearls, clothed in silk in the Gardens.
Opening of the qualities of the successful believers.
Those very believers are the heirs who will inherit Paradise (Firdaws), abiding therein.
Rewarded with the highest place in Paradise for their patience, greeted with welcome and peace.
Abiding therein — a good dwelling and resting place.
Believers who do good will be lodged in lofty dwellings of Paradise beneath which rivers flow — directly follows the mandatory trial verses (29:2-3).
Description of who earns it: those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord.
No soul knows what joy is kept hidden for them as reward for what they used to do.
People of Paradise, that day, are joyfully occupied — follows immediately after the resurrection-evidence passage in the same surah.
Their greeting from a Merciful Lord: 'Peace.'
The righteous led to Paradise in companies; its keepers greet them, 'peace be upon you, you have done well, so enter it, abiding.'
Their response: 'Praise be to Allah who has fulfilled His promise to us' — trust in Allah's promise, central to renewed faith.
'Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, delighted.'
Served with trays and cups of gold, and whatever the souls desire and the eyes find pleasing.
The similitude of the Paradise promised: rivers of unpolluted water, milk unchanging in taste, wine delightful to drinkers, and pure honey.
Paradise brought near for the righteous, not far off.
'Enter it in peace — this is the Day of everlasting life.'
Whatever they wish is theirs, and with Us is even more.
The God-fearing amid gardens and springs.
The God-fearing amid gardens and delight.
Enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord has spared them the punishment of the blazing Fire.
The God-fearing amid gardens and a river.
In an assembly of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent.
Two gardens for whoever fears standing before his Lord — opens Ar-Rahman's Paradise description.
Companions restraining their glances, untouched before them by man or jinn.
'Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness?' — a general, profound principle of reward.
Closing refrain: 'Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of majesty and honor.'
Those brought near, in the Gardens of Delight.
No vain or sinful talk heard therein.
Only the saying: 'Peace, Peace.'
People of the Right Hand: amid thornless lote-trees.
Their companions specially created.
The Day believing men and women see their light running before them: 'good tidings for you today — Gardens beneath which rivers flow' — same surah as the mandatory steadfastness verse 57:16.
Their light will run before them and in their right hands, on the Day Allah will not disappoint the Prophet and those who believed with him.
The righteous drink from a cup mixed with camphor.
Rewarded for their patience with a Garden and silk.
Reclining therein, feeling neither excessive sun nor bitter cold.
The God-fearing have achievement/triumph.
Gardens and vineyards.
The righteous are truly in bliss.
Given to drink a pure, sealed wine.
Faces that day, joyful.
Pleased with their striving.
In a lofty Garden.
Reward with their Lord: Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, abiding forever — Allah pleased with them, and they with Him.

Directly states the purpose for which jinn and humans were created: to worship Allah. For a user whose faith feels shaken, this gives a clear answer to the existential question of why we were created and what our purpose is.
